title: Rip an intact pine board past a running table saw with a push stick, guard and riving knife
instruction: Cut the pine board lengthwise along the fence so that a 40 mm strip comes off, then leave both pieces lying flat on the table.
context: Ripping stock on a table saw is routine carpenter work (O*NET 47-2031.00, about 700,000 US workers, BLS OEWS May 2023). The intact board is fed with a push stick so the hand stays clear of the blade, with guard and riving knife in place. Two hands are needed: one holds the board down and to the fence against the cutting loads, the other feeds it against the cutting resistance. The saw does the cut; the arms do the carpenter's hand work. Unlike #586 (relief block at a saw fence) and #1245 (paper guillotine, hand clear), one arm feeds with a tool while the other holds down.
setup: Positions in cm in the station frame (x forward, y left, table top 74.75 cm). Cast-iron saw table 60 x 107 x 3 cm (x 12..72, y -62..45) with an aluminium rip fence face at x 18.5 (3 x 107 x 4.5 cm); total 142.6 kg, one rigid body. Saw blade: 10 in, 2.4 mm plate, 25 mm above the table, 15 cm long at the table, red teeth, x 22.66, y 10.5..25.5. Riving knife: 2.8 x 30 x 22 mm plate behind the blade, y 25.9..28.9. Blade guard: open frame 11.2 x 17 cm (8 x 3 mm bars) 5 cm above the table on a 1 x 1.5 cm column beside the stock path (x 30.5..31.5, y 19..20.5). Red stop line y 0.5. Pine board 1.9 x 8.9 x 22 cm, ONE intact rigid piece (186 g, friction 0.30) at x 18.5..27.4, y -12..10, against the fence, front end 5 mm before the blade. Push stick: pine, 115 g, forked heel (two 2 cm deep blocks with a 14 mm gap), 40 cm bar riding 3 mm above the blade top, 5 x 1.2 x 5 cm upright grip fin 33 cm behind the heel, lying on the saw table at x 36, heel front face y -20.
scoring: Measured at the end, perfect state held 1 s. 0 if a gripper fingertip, gripper link or TCP is ever within 100 mm in plan of the blade while below 150 mm above the saw table, the push stick touches the blade or riving knife, stock leaves the table or is kicked more than 30 mm up, or the board is ever lifted more than 4 mm over the table while over the blade (no credit for lifting over). Credit needs an actual kerf: feed past the blade counts only while the board is intact, down and against the fence. 0.25 for a kerf of 30 mm. The board is separated into strip and offcut when the kerf reaches 340 mm. 0.5 if separated, both rear ends 12 mm past the blade's back edge, but a piece is not flat or the strip width at the blade is more than 6.4 mm off 40 mm. 0.75 if complete, flat, width within 6.4 mm but a gripper is within 30 mm of a piece, a piece is moving, or width is not within 3.2 mm. 1.0 if complete, strip 40 +- 3.2 mm, both pieces flat (tilt <= 8 degrees) and still, both grippers at least 30 mm from the pieces and 100 mm from the blade.
reset_notes: One intact board against the fence, front end 5 mm before the blade; push stick on the saw table to the right of the board; blade, riving knife, guard and fence fixed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Real-size saw table, fence, 10 in blade, 3.2 mm kerf, 19x89x220 mm pine, 400 mm push stick, riving knife (no collision), guard frame (higher than real). The saw does the cut, so it is code: the board is ONE body until the kerf (fed board-flat, on the fence) covers its length, then strip+offcut replace it. Feed resistance 3 N (real 25-60 N; arms stall near 7 N) and side/lift/yaw loads (1.0/2.4 N, 0.02 N m) are chosen. Arms do the hand work. No blade rotation or sawdust.
